interfaces.name: Stone-crush roots
interfaces.function: Use actual reusable stone and bark to crush roots for later eating, conserving nutrients and age.
interfaces.costs: One actual stone and bark are reserved reusable implements; prepare 1–4 owned roots with two rounds per raw root, one energy per round. Defaults to a nearby eastward worksite; explicit x/y select another actual site. No silent relocation if blocked. New assess-surface/prepare-small operations require separate root-preparation-surface mastery; legacy prepare retains its whole-unit inputs and existing costs. Requirement-level assessment detail and dated assessmentId reads require one additional root-surface-diagnostics study; existing operations retain their previous behavior until that study.
interfaces.effects: Preserve mass, nutrients, toxicity and accumulated spoilage. Crushed food ages at 1.25 baseline. Partial cancellation retains its actual processing fraction and age. No cooking or preservation benefit is implied.

execution.progress: Exact processId, actual site, escrow, reusable tools, paid energy and remaining work. Continue resumes; changing actions or lost reach pauses. Cancel/death releases actual material once without effort refunds.

interfaces.name: Root air drying
interfaces.function: Assemble a reusable stone-and-bark tray, process actual roots and allow weather-dependent drying with reversible preservation while sufficiently dry.
interfaces.costs: Build: two stone units and one bark, two rounds at one energy. Load: up to two original root units, two crushing rounds per raw root at one energy. Already crushed compatible food needs one transfer round, with its prior costs and composition preserved. Unload/dismantle: one round and one energy. Passive weather exchange costs no actor rounds.
interfaces.effects: Food begins at its represented composition or the reviewed 50% root water assumption. Uncovered dry weather at 10–40 C removes at most 0.005 water mass per root per round to fraction 0.12; rain returns up to 0.01 per root, capped at original water. At fraction <=0.12 decay is 0.35 baseline, otherwise crushed food is 1.25 baseline. Exposure continues after unloading. No lost nutrients, reverse spoilage, sterilization or free materials.

execution.progress: Exact processId, actual site, escrow, reusable tools, paid energy and remaining work. Continue resumes; changing actions or lost reach pauses. Cancel/death releases actual material once without effort refunds.

interfaces.name: Small ground-supported root drying
interfaces.function: Assess, build and use a real ground-supported bark sheet with half-unit stone ballast for one 0.1-root drying trial.
interfaces.costs: Assess: site{x,y},stoneIds,barkId,sampleId; one active round and 0.2 energy. Build from your retained assessmentId: reserve the whole actual sheet plus 0.5 stone from named stacks, two active rounds at 0.5 energy. Load supportId/sampleId: exactly 0.1 root, 0.2 proportional work and energy if raw; prior crushing reduces remaining work, with 0.1 transfer effort for fully crushed food. Continue/cancel name processId. Inspect costs one round/0.2 energy; unload or empty dismantle costs one round/0.5 energy.
interfaces.effects: Require an intact connected >=0.2 x0.2 m sheet, actual hard stone >=3, clear reachable firm ground and a safe unspoiled sample. Food area0.16 x0.16 m, exterior ballast margins0.02 m, maximum layer0.003 m. Existing geometry retained; absent geometry uses uncertain square-sheet model density500/thickness0.003. Absent food volume uses uncertain actual mass/density1000. Fragmented or combined separate sheets never become connected. Own body also blocks the site. Completed support has real solid ballast and a non-solid food surface. Passive evaporation is half the existing root rate, at most0.00025 mass/sample/round; wet ground, displaced ballast or collision pauses evaporation, while ageing and rain continue. Existing decay0.35 while actually dry, otherwise1.25; no nutrition/safety bonus. Shared use requires own mastery and actual empty support; living depositor retains food. Unloaded food follows existing loose-food exposure and carrying cost. Interrupted work retains costs; cancellation/death releases surviving partial material on the ground once with source-owner provenance. Empty dismantle/rebuild is paid maintenance, with no automatic wear reset or repair.

shown.question: Can weather-dependent root drying provide a useful safe-food reserve under local conditions?
evidence: Root air drying is personally mastered at tick 122.
Three owned roots remain available at tick 122.
Owned stone totals 1.9 units; no bark is owned.
At tick 122 Ash 2 reported a completed peeling yield of 0.7 bark, with no transfer promised.
The legacy drying tray requires two stone and one bark; insufficiently dried crushed roots age at 1.25 baseline.
shown.uncertainty: A smaller tray's feasibility, material access and practical drying time remain unverified.
shown.goal: Assess a small preservation trial without compromising the safe-food reserve.
completedSteps: Received Ash 2's reported paid bark yield.
outputs: Personal mastery of root air drying.
shown.missing: A feasible physical setup and actual access to its required materials.
shown.next: Request assessment and support for a genuinely smaller drying trial.
shown.benefit: Safe food remains available; preservation benefit is not established.

shown.question: What can a non-ingestive examination establish about the nearby hazelnuts?
evidence: At tick 90, two paid hard-tool work increments confirmed mechanical access to the hazelnut interior.
The retained finding explicitly leaves nutrition, toxicity and safety unknown.
shown.uncertainty: Food safety, nutrition and any useful further processing remain unknown.
shown.goal: Obtain actual mechanical inspection evidence without ingesting unfamiliar food.
completedSteps: Completed paid opening of a 0.1-unit sample with a reusable hard tool.
shown.missing: No safety assay or dietary evidence exists.
shown.next: Share the limited finding; do not ingest hazelnuts based on mechanical access.
shown.benefit: Established mechanical access without an ingestion trial; no dietary benefit established.

shown.question: How does the owned stone respond to a small applied load?
evidence: Tick 61 physical press trial: load 0.3, held true, flexibility 0; consumed 0.1 stone.
shown.uncertainty: Higher loads and practical construction performance remain untested.
shown.goal: Obtain one actual low-cost material measurement.
completedSteps: Tested the identified owned stone stack.
outputs: Verified stone load-response finding for load-band-0.
shown.missing: No further testing required for this limited question.
shown.next: Retain the finding for potential practical use.
shown.benefit: A measured material response is now known.

shown.subject: hazelnut
shown.property: interior mechanically accessible after paid compression
shown.method: two paid work increments with actual hard-tool contact
shown.condition: Only mechanical access; not a food safety assay.

shown.subject: Actual paid bark yield
shown.text: Paid peeling is complete. My two branches yielded 0.7 bark plus one bark-fines unit; I retain one stone and two peeled branches. Separation is personally verified, but this is less than the one bark required by the legacy tray/preparation contracts. I will check the small-batch preparation contract; no material transfer is promised.

shown.subject: Bark extraction trial status
shown.text: I mastered bark-extraction and inspected my two branches: estimated recoverable outer bark mass is 0.22. My inspected stone has a usable edge. I have not yet separated any bark; I will attempt a paid peeling trial next. This is not yet a verified supply or a material commitment.

shown: Root nutrition 14 and berry nutrition 8 are confirmed safe.
Hazelnut mechanical access does not establish food safety.
No preservation benefit has been demonstrated.
